doc.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Becoming Little Satch and lessons from Tony Bruno
summary: He picked up a cornet, was nicknamed Little Satch, and was taught trumpet in the front room by white trumpeter Tony Bruno.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Now what made you want to play the trumpet as a young boy?

It’s a funny story. I always wanted to sing. And I used to go around singing and humming and going on you know [humms], so people called me “Little Satch.” And I didn’t know, and you may not believe this, but they gave us some used instruments from the other high school across town and I picked out the cornet and you wouldn’t believe that I started to play and the first note that I ever played, and the first thing I ever played was “When You’re Smiling” and when I found out that I was playing “When Your Smiling” in seven sharps, so that means push all the valves down, you understand what I mean?

So I learned how to play that, then I learned how to play other songs, and then everyone called me “Little Satch” and I was the big thing around Pensacola. But my mother insisted that I go to this other fella I mentioned, who was named Tony Bruno. And he had been to New York. And one night he heard me play, and he said, “Why don’t you come by my house one day” and — you won’t believe this — he said, “Why don’t you come by my house one day and come to the front door” he said to me. During those days he said to me, “Come to the front door,” and my mother — “and bring your horn.” He ushered me into the living room, during those days, and taught me to play the trumpet.
